prompt:
A small vacuum seal on an electron beam apparatus leaks air into the chamber at a constant rate of 2.50 * 10^16 molecules per second. Take N_A = 6.02 * 10^23 mol^-1.
(a) Calculate the total number of air molecules that enter the chamber in an operating time of 12.0 hours. [2]
(b) Calculate the amount of air, in moles, that enters the chamber during this time. [1]
(c) Assuming dry air has an average molar mass of 29.0 g mol^-1, calculate the total mass of air leaked into the chamber in milligrams. [1]

mark_scheme.criterion: (a) Converts time to seconds: 12.0 * 3600 = 43200 s and multiplies by rate

hints: Remember to convert 12.0 hours into seconds before multiplying by the leak rate.
In (b), divide the total molecules by N_A.
In (c), multiply moles by the molar mass and convert grams to milligrams.
teacher_walkthrough: Review unit prefix conversion: 1 g = 1000 mg.

provenance.abstract_pattern: time-integrated molecular leakage rate to molar and mass accumulation
provenance.independence_statement: Authored as an original medium question on vacuum chamber molecular leakage.
